title: Sweet and energetic 2-year-old Goldendoodle pup, Bruce, seeking a forever home today - NewsBreak
text:
16 hours ago Meet Bruce, the sweet English cream Goldendoodle, looking for love in Florida. Photo by Pet Finder/The Howling Wolf Acres/Edited by Gary Smith Pet parents and dog lovers looking to add a playful companion to their family should consider Bruce, a young Goldendoodle available for adoption through The Howling Wolf Acres in Florida. The two-year-old male pup needs an active household that can match his high energy levels and provide plenty of outdoor adventure.
Bruce is a large standard-size English cream Goldendoodle weighing between 61-100 pounds with a medium-length apricot and beige coat. The neutered male is fully vaccinated, microchipped, heartworm negative, house-trained, and crate-trained. An adoption fee and contract are required for interested families.
A loving Goldendoodle named Bruce is hoping to find a loving home today. Photo by Pet Finder/The Howling Wolf Acres "He is a 2-year-old standard-size English cream Goldendoodle. Bruce has lots of puppy energy and would love an active family/owner with another active dog," the rescue shared in his adoption details .
Bruce Is Great With Other Dogs
The rescue staff shared that this friendly dog thrives in environments with other active dogs and enjoys exploring yards while running and playing with his foster companions. Bruce would do best in a home with another energetic canine friend who can keep up with his puppy-like enthusiasm.
His compatibility with children, cats, and other animals remains unknown at this time.
Bruce ia an energetic English cream Goldendoodle pup Photo by Pet Finder/The Howling Wolf Acres/Edited by Gary Smith "He (Bruce) likes to explore the yard and run and play with the other foster dogs. Bruce is neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and heartworm negative. He is house-trained and perfectly crate-trained," his adoption information said.
The Howling Wolf Acres, located in Longwood, Florida, prepares homeless dogs for adoption through veterinary care, socialization, and training before placing them in suitable homes. Their streamlined adoption process allows potential adopters to visit the Longwood location with their own dogs to ensure compatibility. After meeting Bruce and completing the required contract, approved families can take him home the same day.
Interested families can start the inquiry process by emailing thehowlingwolfacres@gmail.com or calling 321-848-4765 to schedule an appointment. The rescue organization focuses on matching each dog with families where they will thrive long-term, reducing shelter populations while creating meaningful human-animal bonds throughout the Central Florida community.
Bruce represents one of many local dogs waiting for their second chance through private rescue programs working across Florida counties to connect adoptable pets with loving homes.
